questions.q: Define electric current.
questions.explain: Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge. It is measured in amperes (A).

questions.q: State the SI unit of resistance.
questions.explain: The SI unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω). The ampere is the unit of current and the volt is the unit of voltage.

questions.q: A lamp circuit has a fixed voltage. Its resistance increases. Predict the change in current.
questions.explain: Resistance opposes the flow of current. With the same voltage, a larger resistance lets less current flow, so the current decreases.

questions.q: The current through a bulb is measured. State the meter used and its connection.
questions.explain: Current is measured with an ammeter. The ammeter is connected in series so that the same current flows through it and the bulb.

questions.q: The voltage across a bulb is measured. State the meter used and its connection.
questions.explain: Voltage is measured with a voltmeter. The voltmeter is connected in parallel across the bulb.

questions.q: R is resistance, V is voltage, I is current. Identify the formula for R.
questions.explain: Resistance is the voltage across a component divided by the current through it. So R = V ÷ I.

questions.q: A 2 A current flows through a 10 Ω resistor. Calculate the voltage.
questions.explain: Voltage = current × resistance = 2 A × 10 Ω = 20 V.

questions.q: A 12 V supply is across a 4 Ω resistor. Calculate the current.
questions.explain: Current = voltage ÷ resistance = 12 V ÷ 4 Ω = 3 A.

questions.q: A lamp has 12 V across it and 2 A through it. Calculate its resistance.
questions.explain: Resistance = voltage ÷ current = 12 V ÷ 2 A = 6 Ω.

questions.q: A 20 V supply drives 4 A through a heater. Calculate its resistance.
questions.explain: Resistance = voltage ÷ current = 20 V ÷ 4 A = 5 Ω.

questions.q: Ammeters X and Y are in series. X reads 2 A. State the reading on Y.
questions.explain: In a series circuit there is only one path, so the current is the same everywhere. Y reads the same as X, which is 2 A.

questions.q: Two identical bulbs are in series with a 6 V battery. Calculate each bulb's voltage.
questions.explain: In series the supply voltage is shared between the bulbs. Two identical bulbs share 6 V equally, so each has 3 V.

questions.q: Two identical bulbs are in parallel with a 6 V battery. State each bulb's voltage.
questions.explain: Each branch of a parallel circuit is connected across the battery. So each bulb has the full 6 V across it.

questions.q: Two identical bulbs in parallel take 4 A in total. Calculate each bulb's current.
questions.explain: In parallel the total current splits between the branches. Two identical bulbs share 4 A equally, so each takes 2 A.

questions.q: Two identical bulbs in series have 3 V each. Calculate the supply voltage.
questions.explain: In series the voltages across the bulbs add up to the supply voltage. Supply voltage = 3 V + 3 V = 6 V.

questions.q: Two 10 Ω resistors are joined in series. Calculate the effective resistance.
questions.explain: Resistances in series add up. Effective resistance = 10 Ω + 10 Ω = 20 Ω.

questions.q: Two 10 Ω resistors are joined in parallel. Calculate the effective resistance.
questions.explain: Two equal resistors in parallel give half the resistance of one of them. Effective resistance = 10 Ω ÷ 2 = 5 Ω.

questions.q: More resistors are added in series. State the change in effective resistance.
questions.explain: Resistances in series add up. Each resistor added makes the effective resistance larger.

questions.q: State a feature of a series circuit.
choices: each bulb has its own switch
each bulb gets the full voltage
more than one path for current
questions.explain: A series circuit has only one path for the current. If one bulb breaks, the whole circuit stops working.

questions.q: A torch has its cells, switch and bulb in one loop. Name this circuit type.
questions.explain: The cells, switch and bulb are joined one after another in a single loop. This is a series circuit.

questions.q: Lights in homes are wired in parallel. Explain why.
choices: each bulb can be switched separately
questions.explain: In a parallel circuit each bulb is on its own branch. Each bulb can have its own switch, so it can be switched on and off separately.

questions.q: Many appliances are plugged into one socket. Name the hazard this causes.
questions.explain: Many appliances on one socket draw a large total current. The large current heats the cables, and overheating can start a fire.

questions.q: A girl uses a hairdryer with wet hands. Explain why this is dangerous.
questions.explain: Water conducts electricity. With wet hands, current can flow through the girl's body and give her an electric shock.

questions.q: The current through a fuse becomes too large. Describe what the fuse does.
choices: it melts and opens the circuit
it carries current to the earth
questions.explain: A fuse has a thin wire that melts when the current is too large. This breaks the circuit and stops the current.

questions.q: P is power, V is voltage, I is current. Identify the formula for P.
questions.explain: Electrical power is voltage multiplied by current. So P = V × I.

questions.q: A bulb has 9 V across it and 2 A through it. Calculate its power.
questions.explain: Power = voltage × current = 9 V × 2 A = 18 W.

questions.q: A 12 W lamp works on a 6 V supply. Calculate the current.
questions.explain: Current = power ÷ voltage = 12 W ÷ 6 V = 2 A.

questions.q: A 100 W lamp has a current of 5 A. Calculate the voltage.
questions.explain: Voltage = power ÷ current = 100 W ÷ 5 A = 20 V.

questions.q: A hairdryer has a power of 1 kW. Calculate its power in watts.
questions.explain: One kilowatt is 1000 watts. So 1 kW = 1000 W.

questions.q: A 100 W lamp is on for 20 s. Calculate the energy used.
questions.explain: Energy = power × time = 100 W × 20 s = 2000 J.

questions.q: State the unit in which electrical energy is sold to homes.
questions.explain: Electrical energy for homes is sold in kilowatt-hours (kWh). One kWh is the energy used by a 1 kW appliance in 1 hour.

questions.q: A lamp has a power of 500 W. Calculate its power in kW.
questions.explain: One kilowatt is 1000 watts. So 500 W = 500 ÷ 1000 kW = 0.5 kW.

questions.q: A 2 kW air-conditioner runs for 8 h. Calculate the energy in kWh.
questions.explain: Energy in kWh = power in kW × time in hours = 2 kW × 8 h = 16 kWh.

questions.q: A home uses 5 kWh at 20 cents per kWh. Calculate the cost.
questions.explain: Cost = energy used × cost per kWh = 5 kWh × 20 cents = 100 cents.

questions.q: A 2 kW heater uses 6 kWh of energy. Calculate the time it was on.
questions.explain: Time = energy ÷ power = 6 kWh ÷ 2 kW = 3 h.
